categoryNote: Read-only hardware/driver inventory and owner guidance. Driver installation and removal stay separate from optimization: nothing in this category auto-installs, auto-removes, auto-rolls-back or flashes anything. All eleven entries are reports or guidance documents implemented in src/nxcore/functions/NX20.ps1 (Get-Nx20* functions). Detection is reused, not duplicated: Get-NxHardwareReport/Get-NxBuildReport (core), Get-NxGpuAdaptersInternal + vendor status helpers (NX04), Get-Nx07AdapterInventory (NX07), Get-NxDriverInventory (NX16-010, which owns driver inventory mechanics) and Get-NxTweakEligibility (NxCompat, which owns eligibility). Every report carries an uncertainty array (SynToolkit pattern, r4): unavailable data is Unknown, never fabricated; serial numbers are withheld, MACs are masked to the OUI, and serial-like USB instance suffixes are redacted. No entry makes a performance claim.

tweaks.name: Hardware inventory master report
tweaks.description: Read-only master inventory: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, chassis, board, BIOS, firmware mode and build context, with every unavailable value uncertainty-marked.
tweaks.objective: One evidence-backed hardware baseline for reports, eligibility context and the owner support bundle.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Composition entry, not a new detector: CPU/GPU/RAM/storage/chassis come from Get-NxHardwareReport (NxHardware.ps1 - strictly read-only, PCI vendor-ID classification, 64-bit qwMemorySize VRAM with the WMI AdapterRAM >4 GB wraparound handled, junk-SMBIOS sanitization), and this function adds the board/BIOS CIM reads no other category owns (Win32_BaseBoard, Win32_BIOS, Win32_ComputerSystem) plus build context composed from Get-NxBuildReport (NX16-012 owns the build report; composed here, never duplicated). Firmware mode is reported with its source and an ordered fallback chain (PEFirmwareType registry -> firmware_type hint -> Get-ComputerInfo BiosFirmwareType -> Uncertain). Serial numbers are never emitted: serialPresent is reported with serialWithheld=true, the same identifier policy the NX16-017 support bundle applies. Every failed read lands in the uncertainty array and leaves the field null - nothing is fabricated (SynToolkit uncertainty pattern, r4). Consumed by NX20-003/004/005/009/011. Driver enumeration/cleanup does not happen here; NX16-010/011 own those mechanics.
tweaks.defaultState: Information only; no NEXTRIX hardware report exists.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable hardware inventory object (optionally a JSON file in the owner-chosen folder).

verify.procedure: Report object: hardwareReadSucceeded plus computer/board/bios (bios.firmwareType and firmwareTypeSource; serialPresent with serialWithheld=true), cpu/gpu/memory/storage/chassis sections from Get-NxHardwareReport, os build context, categoryPolicy and an uncertainty array. A failed read appears in uncertainty and the corresponding field is null - never a default.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; the optional JSON export is additive.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Writes one JSON report file to the owner-chosen folder only when -OutputFolder is supplied.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (WMI inventory classes; junk-SMBIOS sanitization; qwMemorySize VRAM fix)

tweaks.name: GPU vendor & driver capability report
tweaks.description: Read-only GPU report: adapters, PCI vendor classification, driver version/date/signer, VRAM with its source, present mode and the vendor-status snapshot NX04 gates rely on.
tweaks.objective: Give NX04 and the vendor driver entries one evidence snapshot of which GPU vendors and driver surfaces exist on this machine.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Adapters come from Get-NxGpuAdaptersInternal (NX04) when that module is loaded, otherwise from Get-NxGpuReport (NxHardware) enriched by a single Win32_PnPSignedDriver read; vendor is classified by PCI vendor ID only (VEN_10DE/1002/8086, r4) and a Microsoft Basic Display adapter is recorded as vendor None rather than a real GPU. vendorStatus composes the read-only Get-NxNvidiaStatus/Get-NxAmdStatus/Get-NxIntelStatus helpers (nvidia-smi documented status queries only - per-profile settings are not part of its documented surface) plus Get-NxHagsCapability and Get-NxHybridGraphicsReport when present; an absent module is reported as an explicit 'not loaded' reason, never guessed. The gate itself remains Get-NxTweakEligibility (NxCompat): requiredHardware.gpuVendor is checked against HardwareReport.gpu.vendorsPresent - this report supplies evidence and does not add a second gate. VRAM always carries vramSource; registry qwMemorySize wins over the wrapping WMI AdapterRAM. Driver dates record which source produced them. Feeds NX04-002..023 and NX20-003/004/005.
tweaks.proposedState: GPU capability object (optionally JSON) with vendor gates, adapter detail and vendor-status snapshot.

verify.procedure: Report object: adapters[] each with vendor, driverVersion, driverDate and driverDateSource, vramBytes and vramSource; vendorGates.NVIDIA/AMD/Intel present flags consistent with vendorsPresent; vendorStatus entries are either a snapshot or an explicit not-loaded reason; gateMechanism names NxCompat; uncertainty array present.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Reads nvidia-smi status when present (documented read-only query).
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (PCI vendor-ID classification; AdapterRAM wraparound fix)

tweaks.name: NVIDIA driver management (inventory, guidance, profile inspection)
tweaks.description: Read-only NVIDIA driver/software inventory plus the documented owner-run clean-install workflow; DDU is documented, never downloaded or executed. Profile inspection is honestly reported as unavailable.
tweaks.objective: Let an NVIDIA owner see the installed driver/software state and follow an official-source update/rollback procedure without NEXTRIX touching drivers.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Inventory + guidance, no operation. Detects NVIDIA adapters by PCI vendor ID (requiredHardware.gpuVendor=[NVIDIA] is also mechanically enforced by the compat resolver), reads installed display-driver packages (Win32_PnPSignedDriver joined by DeviceID), vendor software from the uninstall registry (inventory only - it may include non-GPU NVIDIA components, reported as such), and nvidia-smi's documented read-only status surface (driver version/p-state/persistence/compute mode). PROFILE INSPECTION IS HONESTLY ABSENT: NVIDIA per-profile settings live in a proprietary profile store with no documented native read API; NX04-009..016 own that vendor-guidance route, so this report returns profileInspection status NotAvailable rather than reading undocumented stores. Currency is ManualComparisonRequired: both the Windows 4-part driver version and the vendor package version are listed next to the official NVIDIA driver page - NEXTRIX performs no remote lookup and asserts no outdated/current verdict. The clean-install workflow (restore point NX16-002 -> official package -> optional DDU per its own documentation -> installer clean-install option where offered -> reboot -> re-verify -> Device Manager rollback) is documentation for the owner: no download, no install, no removal, no DDU execution, no Driver Store cleanup (that is NX16-011, ADVANCED and per-package consent). driverOperationPolicy returns install/removal/firmwareFlash = NeverAutomated.
tweaks.defaultState: NVIDIA driver/software state as installed by the vendor or OEM.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only before-state report plus vendor-sourced update/rollback guidance; the owner performs any change.

verify.procedure: Report object: supported=true only when an NVIDIA adapter is present (otherwise supported=false with a reason); adapters[] and installedDriverSummary (driverVersions, newest/oldest date, infNames); driverRecords with version/date/signer; vendorTooling shows nvidia-smi availability or an explicit reason; currencyCheck lists both version strings and the official NVIDIA page; cleanInstallGuidance.ownerSteps has the documented workflow; profileInspection.status='NotAvailable'; driverOperationPolicy.install/removal/firmwareFlash='NeverAutomated'. No installation occurred - the journal stays write-free.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no driver operation is performed. If the owner performs an update, rollback means reinstalling the previous vendor package or Device Manager 'Roll Back Driver'; keep the old installer (guidance text states this).

originalState.method: Report itself is the before-state artifact (adapter driver version/date, INF, signer, vendor software versions).

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Reads nvidia-smi status when present; no operation is performed on the driver.
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.
documentationSource: https://www.wagnardsoft.com/ (third-party DDU reference - recorded only, never downloaded or executed)

tweaks.name: Network driver inspection & version report
tweaks.description: Read-only network adapter driver/version report that reuses the NX07 adapter inventory and feeds NX07's advanced-property capability decisions.
tweaks.objective: Separate driver-version evidence from tuning: know which network driver is installed before trusting any adapter-property capability check.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Driver-version/history view of network adapters, reusing Get-Nx07AdapterInventory (NX07-001) so the advanced-property capability map is not duplicated; when the NX07 module is absent it falls back to Win32_NetworkAdapter plus one Win32_PnPSignedDriver read. Reports per-adapter driverVersion/provider/date, physical vs virtual counts, the advanced-property count (not the keyword map itself - that contract stays NX07's), and the NET-class driver records with INF/signer. Read-only: no adapter restart, no advanced-property write, no network stack reset, no netsh invocation. MAC addresses are masked to the vendor OUI in fallback mode. Every failed read is recorded in uncertainty; driver dates are reported as read, never corrected. XREF: catalogue note 'feeds NX07 advanced-property availability'; NX07 owns the tuning decisions, NX20 owns this read-only driver evidence.
tweaks.proposedState: Network driver report object (optionally JSON) per adapter and per NET-class driver package.

verify.procedure: Report object: adapterSource names the reused inventory (NX07 or fallback); adapters[] carry driverVersion/driverProvider/driverDate and advancedPropertyCount; netClassDrivers[] list NET-class records with INF/signer; physicalCount/virtualCount and driverProviders populated; capabilityXref names NX07 ownership; uncertainty array present.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.

tweaks.name: USB hardware inventory report
tweaks.description: Read-only USB inventory: controllers, hubs and present devices with VID/PID, status, problem code and installed driver, with serial-like instance suffixes redacted.
tweaks.objective: Be the single USB inventory owner so NX08 USB troubleshooting and NX09 selective-suspend work never duplicate or contradict it.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Owner of USB hardware inventory (catalogue: NX08-007 cross-references here). Controllers come from Win32_USBController; present USB devices and hubs from the documented Get-PnpDevice cmdlet with role classification (root hub/hub/composite/HID/device), VID/PID, status, problem code and problem text, joined to installed driver records by DeviceID from one Win32_PnPSignedDriver read. Win32_PnPEntity is the documented fallback when the PnpDevice cmdlet is unavailable (with problem detail marked unavailable, not zero). USB serial-like instance suffixes are redacted; VID/PID and bus topology are kept because they are not device identifiers. Inventory only: no device enable/disable, no power-management write, no driver operation, no selective-suspend change (USB selective suspend is NX09-005; USB symptom troubleshooting is NX08-007). Every failed read lands in uncertainty.
tweaks.proposedState: USB inventory object (optionally JSON): controllers, hubs, devices, problem devices and per-class counts.

verify.procedure: Report object: controllerCount/controllers[]; deviceCount/hubCount; devices[] with role, vendorId, productId, status, problem, hasProblem and masked instanceId; problemDevices[]; devicesByClass counts; notes state the NX08-007/NX09-005 cross-reference and inventory-only boundary; uncertainty array present.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.

tweaks.name: Installed driver history report
tweaks.description: Read-only timeline over the installed drivers: newest/oldest, per-year and per-provider counts, unsigned entries and date anomalies.
tweaks.objective: Answer 'what driver state is this machine in' without touching drivers, while leaving inventory mechanics and cleanup to their owners.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Timeline view built ON Get-NxDriverInventory (NX16-010): enumeration, Driver Store size and per-driver fields are reused, never re-implemented (coordination rule: NX16-010/011 own driver inventory and cleanup mechanics; this entry XREFs both). Adds newest/oldest lists, per-year and per-provider counts, unsigned entries, and date anomalies (future-dated or pre-1990 OEM metadata and unparseable dates are reported, never corrected); device instances sharing name/provider/version/INF collapse to one history entry, so a raw PnP enumeration count and the history row count are not the same number. It also verifies completeness against the module's shared read-only driver map and labels inventoryCompleteness (Complete, Partial, Partial-CompletedFromDriverMap, FallbackDriverMap): when the reused enumeration reports a read failure, the history view is marked partial and completed from the shared map instead of presenting a truncated list as complete. Driver Store cleanup is NX16-011 (ADVANCED, per-package explicit consent) and is never proposed or performed here. Read-only; a failed enumeration becomes uncertainty, never a fabricated driver list. This follows the r2 read-only health-verifier pattern: report what is installed, change nothing.
tweaks.proposedState: Driver history object (optionally JSON) with timeline, provider/year summaries, unsigned and anomaly lists.

verify.procedure: Report object: inventorySource names NX16-010 (or the explicit fallback); inventoryCompleteness is Complete/Partial/Partial-CompletedFromDriverMap/FallbackDriverMap with a completionNote whenever the list is not complete; driverCount counts de-duplicated history entries and is at least the reused NX16-010 count; newestDrivers/oldestDrivers are date-sorted; driversByYear/driversByProvider populated; unsignedCount and dateAnomalyCount match their lists; notes state that cleanup is NX16-011; uncertainty array present.

sideEffects: Reads the Driver Store folder size (read-only metadata walk).
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.
documentationSource: r2-atlasos-revios.md (read-only health verifier: report what changed, change nothing)

tweaks.name: Hardware compatibility report generator
tweaks.description: Read-only report in the exact shape NxCompat consumes, plus optional real eligibility evaluation of supplied registry tweaks.
tweaks.objective: One documented bridge between machine facts and eligibility output, so gates are fed by evidence instead of ad-hoc probing.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Generates gateInputs in the exact shape Get-NxTweakEligibility reads (gpu.vendorsPresent, memory.totalGb, storage.hasSsd, chassis.chassisClass, build/insiderChannel/readSucceeded) by composing Get-NxHardwareReport and Get-NxBuildReport. When -Tweaks is supplied it calls the REAL resolver (NxCompat.ps1) per tweak instead of re-implementing any rule, returning eligible/reasons/warnings/riskClass per tweak. It refuses eligibility evaluation - rather than guessing - when hardware/build data is unavailable or NxCompat is not loaded, and records that in uncertainty. No mutation, no eligibility override: the resolver's answer is reported as-is. Hardware uncertainty is carried verbatim (including the storage-class honesty rule where an unreadable class yields hasSsd=false, which the resolver treats as ineligible). This is the report the catalogue means by 'feeds NxCompat eligibility output'; it does not replace NxCompat.
tweaks.proposedState: Compatibility object (optionally JSON) with gate inputs, hardware/build summaries and, on request, eligibility per tweak.

verify.procedure: Report object: gateInputs.gpu.vendorsPresent, memory.totalGb, storage.hasSsd/hasHdd, chassis.chassisClass and build fields populated; hardwareSummary/buildSummary present; eligibilityEvaluated=false without -Tweaks, and with -Tweaks eligibility[] contains the real resolver result per tweak (or a recorded reason why evaluation was refused); uncertainty array present.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.
documentationSource: docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md (capability detection is the primary gate)

tweaks.name: Device configuration inspection
tweaks.description: Read-only per-device inspection: inventory with problem codes, and a documented property set (driver, service, location, hardware ids, parent) for one device.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner and the vendor-driver entries a precise device-level view without Device Manager round-trips or undocumented property writes.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Inventory mode lists present devices with status and problem code/description (bounded by -MaxDevices with totals, optional -Class filter). Detail mode (-InstanceId) reads a documented Get-PnpDeviceProperty allowlist: device/friendly name, class, manufacturer, driver version/date/provider, driver description and INF path, service, problem code, location info, parent, hardware/compatible IDs, install and last-arrival dates; it joins the installed driver record for signer/INF and resolves the parent device name. Serial-number properties are deliberately not read, and instance IDs are masked where they can carry a serial. Read-only: no device enable/disable, no driver update, no property write, no registry write. Per-device IRQ/MSI or other tuning is NX17's scope, not this entry's; a property that is absent for a device is normal and simply omitted (never recorded as an error).
tweaks.proposedState: Device inventory object, or a per-device detail object with the documented property allowlist (optionally JSON).

verify.procedure: Inventory mode: totalDeviceCount/listedDeviceCount/devices[] with status, problem and hasProblem, plus problemDeviceCount. Detail mode: device object (masked instanceId, friendlyName, className, status, problem, driverVersion/date/provider, infName, signer, parent) and properties[] from the documented allowlist; no serial-number property is present; propertyPolicy documents the exclusions; uncertainty array present.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.

tweaks.name: BIOS/version currency guidance (report only)
tweaks.description: Read-only BIOS/board/firmware/Secure Boot/TPM report plus the owner procedure for checking BIOS currency with the OEM; firmware is NEVER flashed by NEXTRIX.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner facts and a safe OEM-sourced procedure instead of an automated firmware path that cannot be made rollback-safe.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Facts + owner procedure only. Reports system/board/BIOS identity, installed SMBIOS BIOS version and release date, firmware mode with source (PEFirmwareType -> firmware_type hint -> Get-ComputerInfo -> Uncertain), Secure Boot, TPM and BitLocker states via documented read-only routes, with denied reads recorded as Uncertain - never as disabled. Currency is ManualComparisonRequired: the owner compares installed version and release date against the OEM support page for the EXACT system model; NEXTRIX performs no lookup and makes no currency verdict (there is no documented programmatic 'is my BIOS current' API - hence E0 by catalogue). updateGuidance enumerates the prerequisites and prohibitions: AC power, no interruption, OEM package only, BitLocker recovery key available / protection suspended where OEM or Microsoft guidance requires it, no third-party/modded images, and no scripting of the flash. Microsoft's documented UEFI firmware update platform (OEM firmware delivered as a driver package, typically via Windows Update) is described, not triggered or blocked. flashingPerformed=false and automationPolicy=NeverAutomated are part of the returned contract.
tweaks.proposedState: BIOS/firmware report object plus an OEM-sourced currency procedure; the owner performs any update outside NEXTRIX.

verify.procedure: Report object: system/board/bios, installedBiosVersion and installedBiosReleaseDate, bios.firmwareType with firmwareTypeSource; secureBoot/tpm/bitlocker states are Read or Uncertain with reasons; currencyStatus='ManualComparisonRequired'; updateGuidance.automationPolicy='NeverAutomated' and flashingPerformed=false; ownerSteps/prohibited lists present. No firmware operation occurred (journal stays write-free).

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no firmware operation is performed; flashing is never automated, scripted or initiated by NEXTRIX.

originalState.method: Report itself is the before-state record (installed SMBIOS version + release date).

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Secure Boot/TPM/BitLocker reads can require elevation; denied reads appear in uncertainty.
Writes one JSON report file only when -OutputFolder is supplied.
